text:
maria: heads up - noticed 95th tail latency flickers on several fractional dedicated slices on host-rack-22 (us-west-1). Correlates with vf0 tx bursts from tenant Y.

samir: saw the spike on scrum dash. spikes align with tenant Y nightly prep jobs? link: https://grafana/redwood/d/latency?var-host=host-rack-22&from=now-2h

olivia: can we confirm whether this is NIC VF contention or upstream TOR? any link-level errors?

maria: ethtool counters show per-vf drops increasing during spike window:
```
eth0:
  vf0: tx_packets 1.2M tx_errors 0 tx_drops 0
  vf1: tx_packets 20k tx_errors 40 tx_drops 5
```

maria: vf1 hosts fractions for other tenants and is experiencing drops. vf0 = tenant Y. vf0 bursts cause VF scheduler latency for vf1.

ben: that matches noisy neighbor by VF scheduling; we dual-homed this NIC for utilization. maybe time to pro-actively partition VF to spare NIC or move vf0 to isolated host.

raj: ops idea: soft-isolate tenant Y by steering to spare-fractional-pool-usw1 for 30m while we probe. This is a higher-cost path but keeps SLOs.

olivia: agree. also add a per-VF irqbalance pinning test in lab before any driver bump. suspect MSI-X allocation issue.

samir: commands to run for quick mitigation:
```
./bin/routectl move --tenant Y --pool spare-fractional-pool-usw1 --reason "vf noisy neighbor" --ttl 1800
ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "vf[01]"
irqbalance --oneshot --cpubind=2,3 --irq 45
```

maria: moving now. infra-bot: audit entry. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: [AUDIT] move invoked by maria for tenant Y -> spare-fractional-pool-usw1 TTL=1800

zoe: +1 on move. tagging @platform-costs because spare-fractional-pool is backed by dedicated-proxy-redwood-burst which is ~3x per-token. Need approval for prolonged steering.

ben: short-term +1. long-term we should evaluate SR-IOV VF quota per host baseline and either: 1) reserve quiet VF lanes for latency-sensitive tenants, or 2) adopt strict VF-to-slice 1:1 carveouts on high-risk hosts. CAPEX vs OPEX tradeoff.

raj: can we instrument a quick experiment to throttle VF0 TX cap to see if backpressure mitigates neighbor impact? ip link has txqueuelen but driver provides per-vf bandwidth shaping via 'nft qdisc' on vf interface.

samir: quick throttle snippet I used in lab:
```
# attach clsact qdisc
tc qdisc add dev vf0 root handle 1: htb default 10
tc class add dev vf0 parent 1: classid 1:10 htb rate 200mbit ceil 400mbit
```

olivia: add telemetry note: log per-slice RPC lat and KV hitrate during throttle window. we'll correlate to see if KVCACHE regen is the hidden amplifer.

maria: post-move notes: tail latency stabilizing on vf1 consumers, overall egress errors didn't go down (driver still logs sporadic flow steer warnings) but SLOs restored.

ben: next steps: schedule controlled driver upgrade on bench, and a preemptive host labeling rule: annotate hosts with 'vf-sensitive=true' so allocation avoids multi-tenant VFs by default.

zoe: platform-costs asked for estimate: if we permanently steer 10 noisy tenants to spare-fractional-pool, OPEX delta ~+$12k/mo. Will escalate if we recommend permanent steer.

maria: I'll attach pcap and ethtool outputs to ticket INFRA-4982. Also will add a short runbook entry for "VF noisy neighbor mitigation" with commands we tested.

raj: thanks. I'll open a PR to add host-labeling to the scheduler and a scheduling guard that prefers 1:1 VF assignment for hosts with label vf-sensitive=true.

infra-bot: [NOTICE] incident INFRA-4982 created by maria (priority P2). Monitors set for 60m.

samir: monitoring 30m window now. will revert move after 30m if stable. ping me for repro with tenant Y team.
